objects.title: Finite-kernel lifting of rational polyhedral domains
objects.model: Faithful rational linear actions on a finite-dimensional rational vector space and its equivariant rational quotient.
objects.statement: If the quotient action has a full-dimensional strong rational polyhedral domain Q, the action kernel K is finite, and D=C intersect p^{-1}(Q) is full-dimensional rational polyhedral with p(D)=Q, then the full action has a strong rational polyhedral domain by finite stabilizer cutting.
objects.quantifiers: Every group, cone and quotient satisfying all stated hypotheses.
assumptions: Full-dimensional rational polyhedral D and exact image p(D)=Q
objects.scope: Dimension-free abstract conditional implication; all geometric inputs remain unpaid for the full mission.
objects.objections: No novelty claim; this does not prove finite kernel or polyhedral D for arbitrary Calabi–Yau spaces.

objects.title: A quotient domain alone does not lift through a degenerate cone
objects.statement: The quotient action on C/T has a strong rational polyhedral domain, but upstairs no convex cone fundamental domain has strong separation; the whole half-plane is a weak domain with infinite stabilizer.
objects.quantifiers: This explicit infinite cyclic group and cone.
assumptions: The fixed boundary line is included in the covered cone
objects.scope: Refutes only automatic abstract quotient-to-full strong-domain lifting.
objects.objections: Not asserted to be a Calabi–Yau fibration; not a counterexample to the user mission.

objects.title: Full closed nef cannot replace effective nef
objects.model: Complex abelian surface A=E×E with End(E)=Z; symmetric 2×2 matrix numerical model.
objects.statement: An irrational rank-one extreme ray of the full closed nef cone meets no rational polyhedral subcone away from zero. Consequently rational-linear translates of such subcones cannot cover the full closed nef cone; that ray is not effective and is absent from its rational hull.
objects.quantifiers: For this explicit abelian surface and any family of rational polyhedral subcones.
assumptions: Standard Rosati identification of N1(A) with symmetric matrices and nef cone with PSD matrices
objects.scope: Geometric obstruction to an overly strong closed-cone formulation.
objects.objections: Does not refute the effective cone conjecture, which is known for abelian varieties; no novelty claim.
